```{r}
#| label: load_all_seasons

# Every season's .rds file lives in this folder - list them all rather than
# reading a single one, so we have every season available to switch between.
season_dir <- here("data", "report_data", "season")

season_files <- list.files(season_dir, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)

# file_path_sans_ext() strips the ".rds", giving us the season id (e.g. "26_27")
season_ids <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(season_files))

# set_names() pairs each file path with its season id, so map() reads every
# file and data_all ends up as a named list: data_all[["26_27"]], data_all[["25_26"]], etc.
data_all <- season_files |>
  set_names(season_ids) |>
  map(readRDS)
```

```{r}
#| label: adding_manager_info

# Same join as before, just wrapped in a function so we can apply it to
# every season's data in one line instead of copy-pasting the imap() block.
add_manager_info <- function(season_data) {
  imap(season_data, \(df, name) {
    if ("manager_id" %in% names(df) && name != "managers") {
      left_join(df, season_data$managers, by = "manager_id")
    } else {
      df
    }
  })
}

data_all <- map(data_all, add_manager_info)
```

```{r}
#| label: season_meta

# A small lookup table: one row per season, with the internal id (e.g. "26_27")
# and the human-readable label (e.g. "2026/27") pulled out of each season's data.
#
# map_chr() (rather than map() + tibble()-per-element) is deliberate here:
# it forces every season's label to be a single string, and will error
# immediately - naming the offending season - if any season's data is
# malformed, instead of silently vanishing the way tibble(x = NULL) does.
season_labels <- map_chr(data_all, \(d) d$season$season_label)

season_meta <- tibble(
  season_id    = names(season_labels),
  season_label = unname(season_labels)
) |>
  arrange(desc(season_id))

# Which season should be pre-selected when the page first loads.
# Falls back to the most recent season if params$current_season isn't found.
default_season <- if (params$current_season %in% season_meta$season_id) {
  params$current_season
} else {
  season_meta$season_id[1]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: filter_short_seasons

# Given one season's list of tables (e.g. data_all[["26_27"]]), find the
# highest gameweek_id across whichever table(s) actually contain that
# column - so we don't have to hardcode a specific table name.
get_max_gameweek <- function(season_data) {
  gw_values <- season_data |>
    keep(\(df) is.data.frame(df) && "gameweek_id" %in% names(df)) |>
    map(\(df) df$gameweek_id) |>
    list_c()

  if (length(gw_values) == 0) {
    return(NA_integer_)
  }

  max(gw_values, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Add a gameweek count onto season_meta, then keep only seasons that
# reached at least gameweek 20.
season_meta <- season_meta |>
  mutate(n_gameweeks = map_dbl(data_all[season_id], get_max_gameweek)) |>
  filter(n_gameweeks >= 20)

# default_season may have pointed at a season we just filtered out (e.g. the
# current season, if it's still early and hasn't reached gameweek 20 yet) -
# re-check it against the trimmed season_meta and fall back if needed.
default_season <- if (default_season %in% season_meta$season_id) {
  default_season
} else {
  season_meta$season_id[1]
}
```

```{r}
#| label: panel_helpers

# Builds the <select> dropdown itself, with one <option> per season.
season_options <- map2(season_meta$season_id, season_meta$season_label, \(id, label) {
  tags$option(
    value = id,
    label,
    selected = if (id == default_season) NA else NULL
  )
})

season_selector <- tags$div(
  class = "season-select-wrapper",
  tags$label("Season: ", `for` = "season-select"),
  tags$select(id = "season-select", season_options)
)

# Given a function that builds one plotly chart from one season's data,
# this generates a hidden <div> per season, each tagged with data-season
# so the JS below knows which one to reveal.
render_season_panels <- function(plot_fn) {
  panels <- pmap(season_meta, \(season_id, season_label, ...) {
    p <- plot_fn(data_all[[season_id]])
    tags$div(
      class = "season-panel",
      `data-season` = season_id,
      style = if (season_id != default_season) "display:none;" else NULL,
      p
    )
  })
  tagList(panels)
}
```

# Reference

```{r}
#| label: season_toggle_script
#| results: asis

cat('
<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const select = document.getElementById("season-select");
  if (!select) return;

  select.addEventListener("change", function (e) {
    const selected = e.target.value;

    document.querySelectorAll(".season-panel").forEach(function (panel) {
      const isMatch = panel.getAttribute("data-season") === selected;
      panel.style.display = isMatch ? "" : "none";

      // Plotly draws charts based on the size of their container at the
      // moment they are created. A chart built while its div is
      // display:none sees a container with zero width/height, so once we
      // reveal it we have to explicitly tell Plotly to recalculate its size.
      if (isMatch) {
        panel.querySelectorAll(".js-plotly-plot").forEach(function (gd) {
          Plotly.Plots.resize(gd);
        });
      }
    });
  });
});
</script>
')
```
